claim: Many orally administered phenolic drugs undergo enterohepatic recycling (EHR), presumably mediated by the hepatic phase II enzymes.
source: Many orally administered phenolic drugs undergo enterohepatic recycling (EHR), presumably mediated by the hepatic phase II enzymes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about phenolic drug disposition.

claim: Certain glucuronides were efficiently recycled by liver.
source: The results showed that certain glucuronides were efficiently recycled by liver.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on experimental results.

claim: OATP1B1/1B3/2B1 were the responsible uptake transporters for hepatic recycling of glucuronides.
source: OATP1B1/1B3/2B1 were the responsible uptake transporters.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on experimental results.

claim: Hepatic uptake is the rate-limiting step in hepatic recycling.
source: Hepatic uptake is the rate-limiting step in hepatic recycling.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on experimental results.

claim: The disposition of many oral phenolics is mediated by intestinal glucuronidation and hepatic recycling.
source: Our findings showed that the disposition of many oral phenolics is mediated by intestinal glucuronidation and hepatic recycling.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on experimental results.

claim: A new disposition mechanism 'Hepatoenteric Recycling (HER)' was revealed, where intestine is the metabolic organ and liver is the recycling organ.
source: A new disposition mechanism 'Hepatoenteric Recycling (HER)", where intestine is the metabolic organ and liver is the recycling organ, was revealed.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental findings.

claim: EHR refers to the recirculation/recycling of endogenous and exogenous compounds involving excretion from liver to small intestine via bile, followed by absorption into enterocytes, which then enters the liver again via portal vein.
source: EHR involves the excretion of substances from the liver to the small intestine via bile, followed by absorption into enterocytes, which then enters the liver again via portal vein (Lennartsson et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a definition supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: EHR is important in the disposition of both endogenous and exogenous compounds.
source: EHR is important in the disposition of both endogenous and exogenous compounds.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: For endogenous compounds (e.g. bile acids), the recirculation through EHR keeps them from being eliminated into the feces and reduces the requirement of daily biosynthesis.
source: For endogenous compounds (e.g. bile acids), the recirculation through EHR keeps them from being eliminated into the feces and reduces the requirement of daily biosynthesis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about bile acid recycling.

claim: For exogenous compounds, EHR prolonged the in vivo exposure and increased their apparent half-life.
source: For exogenous compounds, EHR prolonged the in vivo exposure and increased their apparent half-life.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about drug recycling.

claim: EHR was first conceptualized in the 1950s for bile acid recirculation.
source: EHR was first conceptualized in the 1950s for bile acid recirculation (Norman and Sjovall, 1958).
evidence: This is a historical fact supported by citation.

claim: A variety of drugs are known to undergo EHR, including anticancer drugs (e.g. sorafenib, SN-38), anti-cholesterol drugs (e.g. ezetimibe), anti-osteoporosis drugs (e.g. raloxifene), analgesics (e.g. morphine), and others (e.g. mycophenolic acid).
source: Currently, a variety of drugs are known to undergo EHR, including anticancer drugs (e.g. sorafenib, SN-38), anti-cholesterol drugs (e.g. ezetimibe), anti-osteoporosis drugs (e.g. raloxifene), analgesics (e.g. morphine) Gårdmark et al., 1993, and others (e.g. mycophenolic acid) (Trdan Lušin et al., 2012; Oswald et al., 2008; Ando and Hasegawa, 2005; Vasilyeva et al., 2015; Hasselström and Säwe, 1993).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The enzymes of the microflora present in the intestine are required to hydrolyze the phase II metabolites and regenerate the aglycones for reabsorption.
source: In the case of exogenous compounds, the R in EHR was 'recycling' not 'recirculation,' as the enzymes of the microflora present in the intestine are required to hydrolyze the phase II metabolites and regenerate the aglycones (the parent form of the phase II metabolites) for reabsorption (Williams et al., 1965).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Certain phenolic glucuronides formed in the intestine were efficiently taken up by hepatocytes and then rapidly excreted into the bile.
source: However, we recently found that certain phenolic glucuronides formed in the intestine were efficiently taken up by hepatocytes and then rapidly excreted into the bile (Zeng et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a finding from prior work by the authors, supported by citation.

claim: Glucuronides formed extrahepatically (such as in the intestine), available for hepatic uptake transporters (e.g. Organic Anion Transporting Polypeptides) and subsequently excreted by efflux transporters (e.g. Multidrug Resistance-associated Protein 2), could be recycled by the liver.
source: These phenomena suggest that glucuronides formed extrahepatically (such as in the intestine), available for hepatic uptake transporters (e.g. Organic Anion Transporting Polypeptides) and subsequently excreted by efflux transporters (e.g. Multidrug Resistance-associated Protein 2), could be recycled by the liver.
evidence: This is an inference based on prior observations.

claim: The disposition of phase II metabolites in different metabolic organs (such as liver and intestine) could greatly change with age, gender, and disease conditions.
source: We believe that it is important to delineate HER from EHR since the disposition of phase II metabolites in different metabolic organs (such as liver and intestine) could greatly change with age, gender, and disease conditions (Bolling et al., 2011; Bhatt et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2013; Zhou et al., 2013; Pimentel et al., 2019; Langmann et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: In HER, intestine is the organ for glucuronide formation and liver is the organ for its recycling.
source: In HER, intestine is the organ for glucuronide formation and liver is the organ for its recycling (Figure 1A)
evidence: This is the definition of HER provided in the manuscript, illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: In EHR, liver is the organ for glucuronide formation and intestine is the organ for its recycling.
source: as opposed to in EHR, where liver is the organ for glucuronide formation and intestine is the organ for its recycling (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is the definition of EHR provided in the manuscript, illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Many phenolic drugs and phytochemicals such as flavonoids and polyphenols are significantly metabolized in the human intestine (up to ~70% or more) before entering the liver.
source: The newly proposed HER concept delineates more clearly the disposition mechanism of phenolic drugs and phytochemicals such as flavonoids and polyphenols, which are significantly metabolized in the human intestine (up to ~70% or more) before entering the liver (Patrick et al., 2002; Yang et al., 2012; Strassburg et al., 1998; Kokawa et al., 2013; Sun et al., 2013; Kemp et al., 2002; Kosoglou et al., 2005; Teeter and Meyerhoff, 2002).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The biliary secretion and blood concentrations of Won-7-G reached steady state after 1 hr of infusion and remained steady until 2.5 hr.
source: The biliary secretion and blood concentrations of Won-7-G reached steady state after 1 hr of infusion (Figure 2A1 and A) and remained steady until 2.5 hr.
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 2A1 and A2.

claim: With increased Won-7-G concentrations, both biliary secretion amount and blood concentrations increased.
source: With increased Won-7-G concentrations, both biliary secretion amount (Figure 2A1) and blood concentrations (Figure 2A2) increased.
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 2A1 and A2.

claim: LRE% were significantly lower (p<0.05) at higher infused concentration of Won-7-G.
source: LRE%, calculated by Equation 1, were significantly lower (p<0.05) at higher infused concentration (Figure 2A3).
evidence: This is an experimental finding with statistical significance shown in Figure 2A3.

claim: At lower blood concentrations (<100 μM) of wogonoside, its biliary excretion rates increased linearly.
source: It showed that at lower blood concentrations (<100 μM) of wogonoside, its biliary excretion rates increased linearly.
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 2A4.

claim: At higher blood concentrations (>=100 μM) of wogonoside, biliary excretion rates showed a saturation trend, indicative of transporter-mediated excretion.
source: At higher blood concentrations (>=100 μM), biliary excretion rates showed a saturation trend, indicative of transporter-mediated excretion (Figure 2A4).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with interpretation shown in Figure 2A4.

claim: All seven glucuronides showed a significantly higher (p<0.05) LRE% than their corresponding aglycones.
source: All seven glucuronides (raloxifene has two glucuronides) showed a significantly higher (p<0.05) LRE% than their corresponding aglycones (Table 1, Figure 2B1–B7).
evidence: This is an experimental finding with statistical significance shown in Table 1 and Figure 2B1-B7.

claim: Among the aglycones, wogonin had highest LRE% (41%) when recycled in the form of Won-7-G.
source: Among the aglycones, wogonin had highest LRE% (41%) when recycled in the form of Won-7-G.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the portal vein infusion studies.

claim: Other aglycones showed even lower LRE% (<10%), also in the form of their glucuronides.
source: Other aglycones showed even lower LRE% (<10%), also in the form of their glucuronides.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the portal vein infusion studies.

claim: The uptake of Won was not influenced in the presence of specific transporter inhibitor, while Won-7-G was greatly inhibited, suggesting that aglycone uptake was mainly by passive diffusion.
source: The results indicated that the uptake of Won was not influenced in the presence of specific transporter inhibitor, while Won-7-G was greatly inhibited, suggesting that aglycone uptake was mainly by passive diffusion, and often faster than their corresponding glucuronides.
evidence: This is an experimental finding with interpretation from uptake studies.

claim: LRE% at a higher concentration (100 μM) of Won was significantly lower (p<0.001) than at a lower concentration (2 μM).
source: However, the results indicated that LRE% at a higher concentration (100 μM) was significantly lower (p<0.001) than at a lower concentration (2 μM) (Figure 2C3)
evidence: This is an experimental finding with statistical significance shown in Figure 2C3.

claim: Liver tissue concentrations of wogonin was at least five times higher than won-7-G concentrations.
source: Liver tissue concentrations of wogonin was at least five times higher than won-7-G concentrations (Appendix 2—table 4)
evidence: This is an experimental measurement reported in Appendix 2—table 4.

claim: The slow metabolism in liver was the likely reason for the lower LRE% of aglycones.
source: which indicated that the slow metabolism in liver was the likely reason for the lower LRE%.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the liver tissue concentration data.

claim: LRE% of 16 phenolic-O-glucuronides was highly variable, ranging from 95% to 5%.
source: The results showed that LRE% was highly variable, ranging from 95% to 5%.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from testing 16 glucuronides.

claim: Glucuronidation at 7-position alone is not sufficient to determine if a glucuronide will have high LRE%, suggesting that the aglycone structures are important determinant of its LRE%.
source: In a study of nine 7-O-glucuronides of flavonoids, we were able to show that glucuronidation at 7-position alone is not sufficient to determine if a glucuronide will have high LRE%, suggesting that the aglycone structures are important determinant of its LRE%.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on experimental data from nine 7-O-glucuronides.

claim: There was not sex related differences in the LRE% of Won-7-G and Lut-3'-G.
source: The results indicated that there was not sex related differences in the LRE% of Won-7-G and Lut-3'-G. (Appendix 2—table 6).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from comparing male and female rats.

claim: The LRE% of Bai-7-G increased from ~4% (male rats) to ~10% (female rats) (p<0.05).
source: Interestingly, the LRE% of Bai-7-G increased from ~4% (male rats) to ~10% (female rats) (p<0.05).
evidence: This is an experimental finding with statistical significance from comparing male and female rats.

claim: When given at a low concentration (10 μM), cassette dosing did not significantly impact LRE%.
source: We found that when given at a low concentration (10 μM), cassette dosing did not significantly impact LRE% (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A to D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A to D.

claim: Uptake by three OATP cells varied greatly (p<.005) between glucuronides.
source: We found that uptake by three OATP cells varied greatly (p<.005) between glucuronides (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an experimental finding with statistical significance shown in Figure 3A.

claim: For a particular phenolic glucuronide, their uptake was also significantly different (p<.005) between three OATP-expressing cells.
source: In addition, for a particular phenolic glucuronide, their uptake was also significantly different (p<.005) between three OATP-expressing cells.
evidence: This is an experimental finding with statistical significance from OATP cell uptake studies.

claim: Most glucuronides with high LRE% was taken up rapidly in OATP cells.
source: Moreover, most glucuronides with high LRE% was taken up rapidly in these cells.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from OATP cell uptake studies.

claim: Lut-3'-G could be further metabolized into di-glucuronides of Lut in vivo.
source: The discrepancy can be explained by the fact that Lut-3'-G could be further metabolized into di-glucuronides of Lut in vivo (Kemp et al., 2002).
evidence: This is an explanation supported by citation and confirmed by experimental data.

claim: A liver microsome-mediated metabolism of Lut-3'-G confirmed the formation of Lut di-glucuronides by LC-MS.
source: A liver microsome-mediated metabolism of Lut-3'-G confirmed the formation of Lut di-glucuronides by LC-MS (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: These glucuronides have good affinity to OATP1B1, 1B3, or 2B1 with Km values in the several micro molar range.
source: We found that these glucuronides have good affinity to OATP1B1, 1B3, or 2B1 with Km values in the several micro molar range (Appendix 2—table 7)
evidence: This is an experimental finding from kinetic studies reported in Appendix 2—table 7.

claim: Rifampicin (25 μM) was shown to be potent inhibitor (>90% inhibition) of the uptake of OATP1B1 and OATP 1B3 substrate E2G, Won-7-G, Lut-3'-G.
source: Rifampicin (25 μM) was shown to be potent inhibitor (>90% inhibition) of the uptake of OATP1B1 and OATP 1B3 substrate E2G, Won-7-G, Lut-3'-G (all at 1 μM) (Figure 3C1–C3)
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 3C1–C3.

claim: Rifampicin shown strong pharmacokinetic interactions with atorvastatin and provastatin (classical OATPs substrate) in healthy volunteers.
source: consistent with literature-reports that rifampicin shown strong pharmacokinetic interactions with atorvastatin and provastatin (classical OATPs substrate) in healthy volunteers (Kashani et al., 2009; Riveros et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Telmisartan was shown to be a potent inhibitor (>90%) of the uptake of OATP 2B1 substrate E1S and Lut-3'-G.
source: In addition to rifampicin, telmisartan was also shown to be a potent inhibitor (>90%) of the uptake of OATP 2B1 substrate E1S and Lut-3'-G (Figure 3C3).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 3C3.

claim: If a compound was not an inhibitor of prototypical OATP substrate, it was not a substrate of that OATP.
source: The results showed that if a compound was not an inhibitor of prototypical OATP substrate, it was not a substrate of that OATP (Figure 3D1–D3), but the reverse was not true.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from cross-inhibition studies shown in Figure 3D1–D3.

claim: Substrates of OATP1B1 were able to significantly inhibited (p<.005) the uptake of glucuronides (Won-7-G, E2G, and Lut-3'-G) that are good substrates of a specific OATP.
source: In contrast, substrates of OATP1B1 were able to significantly inhibited (p<.005) the uptake of glucuronides (Won-7-G, E2G, and Lut-3'-G) that are good substrates of a specific OATP.
evidence: This is an experimental finding with statistical significance from cross-inhibition studies.

claim: Aglycones were better inhibitors than their corresponding glucuronides, even though the corresponding glucuronides had higher LRE%.
source: Interestingly, aglycones were better inhibitors than their corresponding glucuronides, even though the corresponding glucuronides had higher LRE%.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from cross-inhibition studies.

claim: 41 out of 44 results (93.2%) from Fisher exact test showed statistical significance for correlation between cellular uptake and LRE%.
source: Of the remaining 44 combinations, 41 out of 44 results (93.2%) showed statistical significance.
evidence: This is a statistical analysis result from Fisher exact test.

claim: Cellular uptake of glucuronides is the rate-limiting step in HER.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrated there were solid correlation between cellular uptake and LRE%. Thus, we showed that cellular uptake of glucuronides is the rate-limiting step in HER.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the correlation analysis between cellular uptake and LRE%.

claim: The correlation between LRE% and intracellular concentration could be mathematically described by an Emax model (Emax 86 ± 17%) with an EC50 value of 42 ± 33 nM.
source: In addition, this correlation (Figure 4) could be mathematically described by an Emax model (Emax86 ± 17%) with an EC50 value of 42 ± 33 nM.
evidence: This is a mathematical modeling result shown in Figure 4.

claim: Compound with a higher LRE% displayed a longer elimination half-life.
source: The elimination half-life was plotted against LRE% (Figure 4; Figure 4—figure supplement 1). Compound with a higher LRE% displayed a longer elimination half-life, which is expected since recycling will inevitably lead to a longer exposure.
evidence: This is an experimental observation with interpretation shown in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The biliary excretion rates of five phenolic glucuronides were similar when five aglycones were given using the small intestine aglycone perfusion or when their corresponding glucuronides were given via direct portal vein infusion.
source: The results indicated that the biliary excretion rates of five phenolic glucuronides were similar when five aglycones (Wog, Bai, Api, Eze, Ral) were given using the small intestine aglycone perfusion or when their corresponding glucuronides were given via direct portal vein infusion.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from comparing intestinal perfusion and portal vein infusion.

claim: The biliary excretion rates of glucuronides from intestinal perfusion were significantly higher than those observed with direct hepatic infusion of aglycones, except for Ral.
source: Moreover, these rates were significantly higher than those observed with direct hepatic infusion of aglycones (Table 1), except for Ral.
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Table 1.

claim: In intestinal perfusion study, the hepatic portal vein blood concentrations of glucuronides are significantly higher (p<0.01) than tail vein blood.
source: In intestinal perfusion study, the hepatic portal vein blood concentrations of glucuronides are also significantly higher (p<0.01) than tail vein blood (Figure 5).
evidence: This is an experimental finding with statistical significance shown in Figure 5.

claim: Small intestine serves as a major metabolism organ for most of the perfused aglycones.
source: These results indicated that small intestine serves as a major metabolism organ for most of the perfused aglycones.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the intestinal perfusion results.

claim: Ral behaved differently because Ral-6-G are formed both in liver and small intestine, and the formation of Ral-6-G in liver is also fast.
source: Ral behaved differently in this study because Ral-6-G are formed both in liver and small intestine. The formation of Ral-6-G in liver is also fast.
evidence: This is an explanation for the different behavior of raloxifene based on experimental observations.

claim: In the presence of OATP transporter inhibitors, the LRE% value of Won-7-G decreased from over ~80% to~40%.
source: In the presence of OATP transporter inhibitors (rifampicin, telmisartan, E2G and E1S at 1000 μM each with 1 hr pretreatment as well), the LRE% value of Won-7-G decreased from over ~80% to~40%
evidence: This is an experimental finding from inhibitor studies.

claim: In the presence of OATP transporter inhibitors, the LRE% value of Lut-3'-G decreased from ~7% to ~3%.
source: and that of Lut-3'-G from ~7% to ~3% (Figure 6A–D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from inhibitor studies shown in Figure 6A–D.

claim: OATP transporters played the major role in the hepatic recycling of Won-7-G and Lut-3'-G.
source: The results indicated that OATP transporters played the major role in the hepatic recycling of Won-7-G and Lut-3'-G, which is consistent with the results in the cell uptake study.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the inhibitor study results.

claim: Other uptake transporters could also participate in the recirculation of the glucuronides since LRE% could not be inhibited by more than 80%.
source: However, since we could not inhibit the LRE% by more than 80%, other uptake transporters could also participate in the recirculation of the glucuronides.
evidence: This is an inference based on the incomplete inhibition observed in the experiments.

claim: After 2.5 hr of incubation, the relative stability of Won-7-G, Api-7-G, and Bai-7-G remained over 80% in 2 μM, 10 μM, and 25 μM.
source: After 2.5 hr of incubation, the relative stability of Won-7-G, Api-7-G, and Bai-7-G remained over 80% in 2 μM, 10 μM, and 25 μM (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from blood stability test shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: HER differs significantly from EHR in that intestine is the main metabolite forming organ and liver is the recycling organ.
source: HER (Figure 1A) differs significantly from EHR (Figure 1B) associated with bile acids and certain drugs, in that intestine is the main metabolite forming organ and liver is the recycling organ.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study defining the new HER mechanism.

claim: EHR of bile acids and various drugs is associated with metabolites that are generated in liver and recycled in intestine.
source: Previously, EHR of bile acids and various drugs (Nielsen et al., 2009) is associated with metabolites that are generated in liver and recycled in intestine.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Unlike EHR of bile acids, hepatic (e.g. OATPs) but not intestinal uptake transporters (e.g. ASBT) appears to be the rate-limiting step in determining the LRE% in HER.
source: and (3) unlike EHR of bile acids, hepatic (e.g. OATPs) but not intestinal uptake transporters (e.g. ASBT) appears to be the rate-limiting step in determining the LRE% in HER.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: Due to the presence of HER, hepatic transporters (e.g. OATPs) will often determine the plasma concentrations of glucuronides, and play a much more important role than the relevant hepatic enzymes (e.g. UGTs) in determining how much glucuronides are excreted into the bile and participate in recycling.
source: Due to the presence of HER, hepatic transporters (e.g. OATPs) will often determine the plasma concentrations of glucuronides, and play a much more important role than the relevant hepatic enzymes (e.g. UGTs) in determining how much glucuronides are excreted into the bile and participate in recycling.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the implications of HER based on the experimental findings.

claim: For orally administered dietary phenolics such as wogonin and drugs such as ezetimibe with high LRE%, double peaks caused by HER were observed in their plasma profiles.
source: For orally administered dietary phenolics such as wogonin and drugs such as ezetimibe with high LRE%, double peaks caused by HER were observed in their plasma profiles (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A to 3D)
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3A to 3D.

claim: A high LRE% means that a phenolic could have double peaks in their plasma profile and a longer terminal half-life.
source: A high LRE% means that a phenolic could have double peaks in their plasma profile and a longer terminal half-life.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the pharmacokinetic implications of high LRE%.

claim: For extrahepatically generated glucuronides, HER is critically important because almost every glucuronides tested were more likely to be excreted into bile if they are given as glucuronides vs corresponding aglycones into the portal vein.
source: In other words, for extrahepatically generated glucuronides, HER is critically important because almost every glucuronides we tested were more likely to be excreted into bile if they are given as glucuronides vs corresponding aglycones into the portal vein (Figure 2B1–B7).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings shown in Figure 2B1–B7.

claim: HER is much more important than EHR for orally administered phenolics whose major metabolic pathway is rapid intestinal glucuronidation.
source: Therefore, we believe that HER is much more important than EHR for orally administered phenolics whose major metabolic pathway is rapid intestinal glucuronidation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings and interpretation.

claim: In chemically induced colitis model, small intestinal UGTs were significantly downregulated but hepatic UGTs were not.
source: For example, in chemically (e.g. trinitrobenzene sulfonic acid) induced colitis model, small intestinal UGTs were significantly downregulated but hepatic UGTs were not (Zhou et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: In hepatitis C, hepatic CYPs, OATPs, OCTs and UGTs were all downregulated.
source: On the other hand, in hepatitis C, where hepatic CYPs, OATPs, OCTs (Nakai et al., 2008) and UGTs (Smolders et al., 2016) were all downregulated
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: HER will shuttle more phenolic compounds and their metabolites, both beneficial and toxic to the colon.
source: Firstly, HER will shuttle more phenolic compounds and their metabolites, both beneficial and toxic to the colon.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the implications of HER.

claim: There is no known mechanism that can rapidly take up glucuronides in the small intestine.
source: This is because there is no known mechanism that can rapidly take up glucuronides in the small intestine.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Some toxic phenolic metabolites can be further biotransformed by the microbial enzymes to more potent toxins.
source: In contrary, some of the toxic phenolic metabolites can be further biotransformed by the microbial enzymes to more potent toxins (Koppel et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The use of phenolics to maintain and improve the health of microbiota is an important future research goal.
source: Therefore, the use of phenolics to maintain and improve the health of microbiota is an important future research goal.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research directions.

claim: If we only recognize the importance of EHR, it would be difficult to understand why inhibition of hepatic UGTs does not always increase aglycone concentration and decrease glucuronide concentration in the blood.
source: For example, if we only recognize the importance of EHR, if would be difficult to understand why inhibition of hepatic UGTs does not always increase aglycone concentration and decrease glucuronide concentration in the blood.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the implications of recognizing HER vs EHR.

claim: If we recognize that a phenolic is mainly processed by HER, an inhibitor that only inhibit liver UGTs is not expected to affect plasma concentrations of orally administered aglycone and its glucuronides as long as intestine is the metabolite forming organ.
source: If we recognize that a phenolic is mainly processed by HER, an inhibitor that only inhibit liver UGTs is not expected to affect plasma concentrations of orally administered aglycone and its glucuronides as long as intestine is the metabolite forming organ.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the implications of HER for drug-drug interactions.

claim: The plasma concentrations of both an aglycone and its glucuronide (if both are substrates of OATPs) or just glucuronide (if only glucuronide is substrate of OATPs), could increase by a drug that did not affect intestinal or liver UGT enzymes.
source: In contrast, the emerging role of OATPs means that the plasma concentrations of both an aglycone and its glucuronide (if both are substrates of OATPs) or just glucuronide (if only glucuronide is substrate of OATPs), could increase by a drug that did not affect intestinal or liver UGT enzymes.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the implications of HER for drug-drug interactions.

claim: The proposed HER mechanism should help determine the dominating mechanism by which drug-drug interactions occur to influence the plasma concentrations of a phenolic aglycone and its glucuronides that are formed in the intestine.
source: Therefore, the proposed HER mechanism should help us determine the dominating mechanism by which drug-drug interactions occur to influence the plasma concentrations of a phenolic aglycone and its glucuronides that are formed in the intestine.
evidence: This is a speculation about the utility of the HER concept.

claim: The influence of HER is more significant when the glucuronides are pharmacologically active (i.e. ezetimibe and dabigatran) or can inhibit CYP enzymes (i.e. gemfibrozil and clopidogrel).
source: This influence is more significant when the glucuronides are pharmacologically active (i.e. ezetimibe and dabigatran [Jia and Zhao, 2011; Jiang and Li, 2010]) or can inhibit CYP enzymes (i.e. gemfibrozil and clopidogrel [Sivapathasekaran et al., 2010; Mutwil et al., 2010]).
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by citations to examples.

claim: Factors that alter the UGT expression in small intestine will significantly influence the recycling of the compounds and their in vivo exposure.
source: Since small intestinal UGTs play a significant role in the HER of the compounds, factors that alter the UGT expression in small intestine will significantly influence the recycling of the compounds and their in vivo exposure.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the implications of HER.

claim: Pathological conditions will greatly influence the intestinal UGTs expression level and thus change the in vivo exposure of a phenolic whose disposition is controlled by a HER process.
source: The results indicated that pathological conditions will greatly influence the intestinal UGTs expression level and thus change the in vivo exposure of a phenolic whose disposition is controlled by a HER process.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on literature search results.

claim: When infused directly into the portal vein, the vast majority of glucuronides of wogonin and ezetimibe reached bile, displaying a highly efficient recycling (LRE%).
source: First, our data showed that when infused directly into the portal vein, the vast majority of their glucuronides reached bile, displaying a highly efficient recycling (LRE%) (Appendix 2—table 5).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supporting the HER mechanism.

claim: Portal vein concentrations of glucuronides were much higher than the corresponding aglycones in the rat intestinal perfusion studies.
source: For those compounds, portal vein concentrations of glucuronides were much higher than the corresponding aglycones in the rat intestinal perfusion studies (Figure 5).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 5.

claim: Direct portal vein infusion of aglycone was substantially less effective in producing biliary excretion of glucuronides than their corresponding glucuronides.
source: Second, direct portal vein infusion of aglycone was substantially less effective in producing biliary excretion of glucuronides than their corresponding glucuronides (Figure 2B1–B7).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 2B1–B7.

claim: Hepatic OATPs took up these glucuronides in a saturable process that can be inhibited by OATP inhibitors.
source: Third, hepatic OATPs took up these glucuronides in a saturable process that can be inhibited by OATP inhibitors (Figure 3B, Figure 3C1–C3).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3C1–C3.

claim: The structural differences between phenolic-glucuronides had a substantial impact on the LRE%.
source: Fourth, the structural differences between phenolic-glucuronides had a substantial impact on the LRE%.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from testing multiple glucuronides.

claim: The term HER properly describes the determining disposition processes of wogonin and ezetimibe.
source: Taken together, these results showed clearly that intestine is the glucuronide forming organ, and liver is the glucuronide recycling organ for these two compounds. Hence, the term HER properly describes the determining disposition processes of these two compounds, a naturally occurring polyphenol flavonoid and a prescription drug, which share minimal structural similarity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: HER could be broadly applicable to other phenolic phytochemicals and drugs.
source: The latter suggest that HER could be broadly applicable to other phenolic phytochemicals and drugs.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the findings with structurally diverse compounds.

claim: The new HER disposition process could explain the pharmacokinetic behaviors of many phenolic drugs, including ezetimibe, raloxifene and diclofenac.
source: The new HER disposition process could explain the pharmacokinetic behaviors of many phenolic drugs, including ezetimibe, raloxifene and diclofenac.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the broader applicability of HER.

claim: All three drugs (ezetimibe, raloxifene and diclofenac) were rapidly glucuronidated by intestinal microsomes and had a double peak PK profiles.
source: All three drugs were rapidly glucuronidated by intestinal microsomes and had a double peak PK profiles (Watanabe et al., 1983; Herz and Bläsig, 1974).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: For diclofenac, extensive intestinal glucuronidation by microsomes with >95% glucuronides formation are consistent with it undergoing through HER instead of EHR.
source: For diclofenac, extensive intestinal glucuronidation by microsomes (Bläsig et al., 1973) with >95% glucuronides formation (Herz and Bläsig, 1974), are consistent with it undergoing through HER instead of EHR.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on literature data supported by citations.

claim: The recycle properties of ezetimibe reported in human was consistent with the proposed HER hypothesis.
source: In addition, the recycle properties of ezetimibe reported in human (Christoffersen et al., 2015) was consistent with the proposed HER hypothesis.
evidence: This is stated as supporting evidence from literature supported by citation.

claim: Over 80% of ezetimibe was converted into glucuronides in intestine with a second peak in its PK profile attributable to hepatic recycling.
source: As over 80% of ezetimibe was converted into glucuronides in intestine (Christoffersen et al., 2015) with a second peak in its PK profile attributable to hepatic recycling.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: For compounds with extensive intestinal glucuronidation and hepatic recycling, HER will fully explain their pharmacokinetic behaviors.
source: Therefore, for compounds with extensive intestinal glucuronidation and hepatic recycling, HER will fully explain their pharmacokinetic behaviors.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings and literature examples.

claim: Lut-G and Ica-G were further metabolized in liver, forming di-glucuronides of Lut and di-glucuronides of Ica, respectively, rendering the original glucuronides unavailable for biliary excretion.
source: We found that these two glucuronides were further metabolized in liver, forming di-glucuronides of Lut and di-glucuronides of Ica, respectively, rendering the original glucuronides unavailable for biliary excretion.
evidence: This is an experimental finding explaining the discrepancy for Lut-G and Ica-G.

claim: A maximum of 50% inhibition of Won-7-G and Lut-3'-G LRE% could be achieved in portal vein infusion experiment with OATP inhibitors.
source: This is because we could only achieve a maximum of 50% inhibition of Won-7-G and Lut-3'-G LRE% in portal vein infusion experiment (Figure 6).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 6.

claim: Transporters belong to the OAT3 subfamily likely contributed to liver uptake of glucuronides.
source: It is likely that transporters belong to the OAT3 subfamily contributed to their liver uptake, since several flavonoid glucuronides were shown to be substrates of OAT3 (Rees et al., 2012), which is also expressed in the liver (Nema et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a speculation based on literature evidence supported by citations.

claim: Good uptake of glucuronides by the OATPs will correlate with high LRE%, as long as the glucuronides taken up by the hepatocytes are not further metabolized.
source: The empirical evidence supports the hypothesis that good uptake of glucuronides by the OATPs will correlate with high LRE%, as long as the glucuronides taken up by the hepatocytes are not further metabolized.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: HER potential can be readily estimated using OATP overexpressing cells and confirmed using the portal vein perfusion model.
source: Because the direct portal vein infusion method is convenient to use with cassette dosing (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), HER potential can be readily estimated using OATP overexpressing cells and confirmed using the portal vein perfusion model.
evidence: This is a methodological conclusion based on the experimental approach.

claim: The portal vein perfusion model should allow medicinal chemists to design new compounds with primarily intestinal glucuronidation that are tailored to treat intestinal, especially colonic diseases.
source: The latter should allow medicinal chemists to design new compounds with primarily intestinal glucuronidation that are tailored to treat intestinal, especially colonic diseases.
evidence: This is a speculation about future applications of the HER concept.

claim: A new disposition terminology HER has been proposed to describe and delineate more clearly the disposition of dietary phenolics and phenolic drugs that are taken orally with intestine as their major metabolism organ and liver as their major recirculating organ.
source: In conclusion, a new disposition terminology HER has been proposed to describe and delineate more clearly the disposition of dietary phenolics and phenolic drugs that are taken orally with intestine as their major metabolism (i.e. glucuronidation) organ and liver as their major recirculating organ.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study.

claim: The new HER terminology more accurately captures the recycling of relevant phenolics, similar to the use of 'EHR' to capture the recycling of bile acids, where the liver is the metabolism organ and intestine as the recycling organ.
source: The new terminology more accurately captures the recycling of relevant phenolics, similar to the use of 'EHR' to capture the recycling of bile acids, where the liver is the metabolism organ and intestine as the recycling organ.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the utility of the new terminology.

claim: The new HER definition could help predict the potential drug-drug interactions under pathological conditions.
source: When combined together, the new HER definition could help predict the potential drug-drug interactions under pathological conditions.
evidence: This is a speculation about the utility of the HER concept.

claim: HER may help to delineate drug-drug interaction mechanisms involving intestinal UGT enzymes and hepatic transporters of glucuronides.
source: It may also help to delineate drug-drug interaction mechanisms involving intestinal UGT enzymes and hepatic transporters of glucuronides, a major challenge that we are still facing today because of all the complexity involved.
evidence: This is a speculation about the utility of the HER concept.
